questions.title: Popped Order of a Stack
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] poppedOrder(int[] values)

Push every value onto an explicit stack (java.util.ArrayDeque works as one), then pop everything off. Return the values in the order they are popped — the harness prints them for you.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the popped values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000 <= values[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Balanced Parentheses
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isBalanced(String s)

Return 1 if the brackets in s are balanced, 0 otherwise. Bracket types are (), [] and {}. Non-bracket rules do not apply — s contains only bracket characters. Use a stack: push opening brackets, match every closing bracket against the top.

Input Format:
One line: the bracket string s.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if balanced, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains only the characters ()[]{}

questions.title: Top After Pushes and Pops
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int topAfterPops(int[] pushes, int pops)

Push every value in order, then pop pops times. Return the value left on top. pops is always strictly smaller than the number of pushes, so the stack is never empty at the end.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and pops.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the top value after the operations.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= pops < n

questions.title: Next Greater Element
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] nextGreater(int[] a)

For each element, find the nearest element to its right that is strictly greater; if none exists use -1. Solve it with a stack for the intended O(n) walkthrough.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with n answers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Sum of Popped Values
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long sumPopped(int[] values, int pops)

Push every value, then pop pops times and return the sum of the popped values. pops never exceeds the number of pushes.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and pops.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the sum of the popped values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= pops <= n
-1000 <= values[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Apply Backspace Characters
questions.description:
A keyboard is stuck: every '#' in the typed stream is a backspace that deletes the last character still on the page. The editor itself is a stack — model it that way.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String applyBackspaces(String s)

Process s left to right. A normal character is pushed onto the stack; '#' pops the last character if any. Return the final text (guaranteed non-empty).

Input Format:
One line: the typed string s.

Output Format:
One line: the final text after applying all backspaces.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains lowercase letters and '#'
the final text is guaranteed non-empty
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= s.length <= 1000, lowercase letters and '#', final text non-empty

questions.title: Browser Back Button
questions.description:
A browser keeps visited pages on a history stack. Every new page is pushed; pressing Back pops the current page.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int currentPage(int[] visits, int backs)

Push the page ids in visiting order, then press Back backs times (a Back press on an empty history does nothing). Return the current page id, or -1 if the history is empty.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and backs.
Line 2: n space-separated page ids.

Output Format:
One line: the current page id or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= backs <= n
1 <= visits[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Bracket Checker for Config Files
questions.description:
A deployment tool validates config snippets: every opening bracket must be closed by the matching type in LIFO order. Letters, digits and operators may appear between brackets and are ignored.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int validConfig(String s)

Return 1 if all brackets (), [] and {} in s are balanced and correctly nested, else 0.

Input Format:
One line: the config string s.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if valid, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains letters, digits, operators and the brackets ()[]{}

questions.title: Warehouse Crate Stack
questions.description:
A loading dock stacks crates on top of each other; only the top crate can be removed. The dock manager wants to know which crate is on top after some removals.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int topCrate(int[] crates, int removed)

Push the crate ids in arrival order, then remove removed crates from the top. Return the id now on top, or -1 if the stack is empty.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and removed.
Line 2: n space-separated crate ids.

Output Format:
One line: the top crate id or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= removed <= n
1 <= crates[i] <= 9999

questions.title: Warmer Days Ahead
questions.description:
A weather service reports, for each day, how many days one must wait until a strictly warmer temperature arrives.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] warmerDays(int[] temps)

For each index i, return the number of days until a temperature strictly greater than temps[i] occurs; if no warmer day exists, return 0 for that day.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated temperatures.

Output Format:
One line with n answers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= temps[i] <= 100

questions.title: Reverse a String Using an Explicit Stack
questions.description:
A message encoder reverses short tokens by pushing characters onto a stack and popping them back — LIFO order reverses the text.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String reverseWithStack(String s)

Push every character of s onto an explicit stack, then pop them all off to build the reversed string. Do not use StringBuilder or library reverse helpers — the stack does the work.

Input Format:
One line: the string s.

Output Format:
One line: s reversed.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains printable non-space characters

questions.title: Min Stack After Operations
questions.description:
A trading terminal keeps a min-stack: alongside the normal stack it remembers the minimum of everything currently stored, so the minimum survives pops.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minAfterOps(int[] pushes, int pops)

Simulate pushing every value in order, then popping pops values. Return the minimum of the values still on the stack (guaranteed non-empty). Use an auxiliary stack of running minimums so both push and pop stay O(1).

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and pops.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the current minimum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= pops < n
-10000 <= pushes[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Valid Stack Sequence
questions.description:
A warehouse robot records the order crates were pushed onto a stack and the order they were popped. You must check whether one pop schedule is consistent with the push order.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int validSequence(int[] pushed, int[] popped)

Return 1 if popped could be the result of pushing pushed in order onto one stack and popping at arbitrary moments (each value popped exactly once), else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated pushed values.
Line 3: n space-separated popped values.

Output Format:
One line: 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
pushed and popped are permutations of the same n distinct values
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, pushed and popped are permutations of the same distinct values

questions.title: Sort a Stack with Another Stack
questions.description:
A buffets stack plates idiosyncratically; the dishwasher sorts a pile using only stack moves — popping plates onto a spare stack and back.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] sortStack(int[] a)

Using stack operations only (push/pop between two stacks), arrange the plates so that popping yields ascending order. Return the values in pop order (i.e. sorted ascending).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-10000 <= a[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Redundant Brackets in Expressions
questions.description:
A formula engine flags expressions where a pair of parentheses wraps nothing useful — like (a) or the outer pair of ((a+b)). A stack scan finds them.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int hasRedundant(String expr)

Return 1 if expr contains at least one pair of parentheses that encloses no operator (only one operand or nothing), else 0. Operands are single letters; operators are + - * /.

Input Format:
One line: the expression expr.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if a redundant pair exists, else 0.

Constraints:
3 <= expr.length <= 1000
expr contains lowercase letters, the operators + - * / and parentheses

questions.title: Celebrity at the Party
questions.description:
At a party everyone is stacked in a lineup. A celebrity is known by everybody but knows nobody. Pairwise eliminations with a stack shrink the candidates to one.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int findCelebrity(int[][] know)

know[i][j] is 1 if person i knows person j, else 0. Return the index of the celebrity (known by all others and knowing nobody), or -1 if there is none.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: n space-separated values of the matrix.

Output Format:
One line: the celebrity index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50
know[i][i] = 0

questions.title: Evaluate Postfix Expression
questions.description:
A RPN calculator on an industrial controller evaluates postfix expressions with an operand stack.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long evalPostfix(String[] tokens)

Evaluate the postfix expression. Operators are + - * / with integer division truncating toward zero (Java's / on longs). Operands may be negative. All intermediate values fit in a long.

Input Format:
One line: the space-separated tokens of the postfix expression.

Output Format:
One line: the result.

Constraints:
1 <= number of tokens <= 100
operands fit in int, operators are + - * /
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= tokens <= 100, operands fit in int, operators + - * /

questions.title: Stock Span Problem
questions.description:
A broker terminal shows, for each day, the stock span: how many consecutive days (including today) the price has been at most today's price.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] stockSpan(int[] prices)

For each day compute the span using a stack of previous days: span[i] = distance to the previous strictly greater price (or i + 1 if none).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated prices.

Output Format:
One line with n spans, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= prices[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram
questions.description:
A laser cutter computes the largest rectangle that fits entirely under a histogram of bar heights. The classic monotonic-stack pass solves it in O(n).

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long largestRectangle(int[] h)

Return the maximum rectangular area under the histogram, where a rectangle spans contiguous bars and its height is the shortest bar in the span.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated bar heights.

Output Format:
One line: the maximum area.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= h[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Colliding Asteroids
questions.description:
Asteroids drift along a lane: positive values move right, negative values move left. When two asteroids meet, the smaller one explodes; if equal, both explode; same-direction asteroids never collide.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] survivingAsteroids(int[] a)

Simulate the lane with a stack and return the surviving asteroids left to right (guaranteed non-empty for every input).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated non-zero integers.

Output Format:
One line with the survivors, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= |a[i]| <= 10000
at least one asteroid survives
